articles.title: iPhone Utra : Apple pourrait déjà s'emparer de 25 % du marché dès 2026
articles.text:
Apple n'a encore commercialisé aucun smartphone pliant que les analystes lui prêtent déjà un impact massif sur ce segment. Selon Counterpoint Research, un pliant sur quatre vendu dans le monde cette année pourrait être signé de la marque à la pomme.
Les analystes de Counterpoint Research ont publié cette semaine leurs projections pour le marché mondial des smartphones pliants en 2026. Longtemps attendu sur ce segment, Apple devrait contribuer à la croissance globale des livraisons alors que son premier modèle pliant doit faire ses débuts sur un marché déjà occupé par plusieurs constructeurs, parmi lesquels Samsung, Huawei ou encore HONOR. La firme à la pomme parviendra-t-elle à tirer son épingle du jeu ? Oui, selon le cabinet d'études.
Un marché des smartphones pliants attendu en forte croissance
Le marché mondial des smartphones pliants devrait rudement accélérer en 2026. Le cabinet d'études Counterpoint Research anticipe une progression de 21 % des livraisons sur un an, portée notamment par l'arrivée du géant de Cupertino sur ce segment. Cette nouvelle concurrence devrait renforcer la bataille sur le marché des modèles pliables haut de gamme au format livre.
Samsung conserverait toutefois sa position de leader mondial. Sa part de marché passerait néanmoins de 40 % en 2025 à 32 % en 2026, toujours selon les estimations du cabinet. La marque à la pomme ferait, de son côté, directement son entrée à la deuxième place avec 25 % des livraisons prévues.
Elle devancerait ainsi de peu Huawei, dont la part devrait reculer à 24 %, contre 30 % un an plus tôt. Motorola arriverait ensuite avec 8 %, contre 12 % en 2025, tandis que HONOR passerait de 7 % à 3 %. Les autres fabricants se partageraient les 8 % restants, contre 11 % l'année précédente.
Apple s'apprête à jouer les trouble-fêtes sur le marché des pliants
L'arrivée de l'iPhone Ultra pourrait donc rapidement bouleverser la hiérarchie du marché jusqu'alors établie. D'après Counterpoint Research, le modèle à écran pliable d'Apple contribuerait à lui seul à faire progresser les volumes mondiaux en 2026, alors que Samsung resterait en tête malgré le recul de sa part.
Le cabinet estime également que les smartphones pliants au format livre pourraient prendre davantage d'importance à mesure que les usages liés à l'intelligence artificielle se développent. Les écrans plus grands et les formats plus flexibles seraient particulièrement adaptés à des tâches comme la synthèse de documents, la modification de contenus, la gestion d'agendas ou encore le transfert d'informations entre plusieurs applications.
Samsung a récemment présenté sa nouvelle génération de smartphones pliants, avec en tête d'affiche la principale nouveauté de cette cuvée 2026 : le Galaxy Z Fold8. Son format plus court et plus large rappelle justement celui qui est souvent évoqué pour le futur iPhone Ultra. Une ressemblance que Drew Blackard, responsable des produits mobiles chez Samsung, a toutefois qualifiée de coïncidence, expliquant que le nouveau design avait été pensé pour proposer une surface d'affichage plus large, notamment pour regarder des vidéos.

articles.title: Steam Deck price hike has completely destroyed sales, new data suggests
articles.text:
Death of Gaming: Just like any other company dealing in hardware products built from off-the-shelf components, Valve is facing some truly difficult choices when it comes to pricing. The company tried to fend off the chip shortage caused by the AI boom with a massive price increase, but potential customers apparently responded by removing themselves from the buying equation.
A recent report by Boiling Steam might confirm what most enthusiasts have always suspected: an overpriced Steam Deck is never going to sell well. In fact, Valve's handheld machine might have already suffered a disastrous drop in sales. Despite the price hike, Valve is earning far less money than it did before.
Boiling Steam used the same methodology it employed to estimate Steam Machine sales, tracking data points from Steam's own global list of best-selling games and products. The outlet compared the Steam Deck's ranking throughout 2025, when it was often listed fairly high on the sales chart. Things changed in 2026, when Valve decided to retire the older – and cheaper – LCD models and offer only the OLED models at a significantly higher price.
At first, OLED Steam Decks appeared to sell out despite the $300 price hike. According to new estimates from Boiling Steam, sales have now undergone yet another dramatic change. Valve is selling 82% fewer units than it did in 2025. Steam Deck sales have allegedly fallen from 11,000 – 18,000 units per week to an average of 1,400 – 3,000 units per week.
Valve tried to offset the massive increase in component prices by passing the supply-chain surcharge on to customers. According to Boiling Steam's estimates, the company is now suffering from a 72% drop in revenue as well. Despite the price hike, Valve might have significantly diminished the Steam Deck's appeal as an enticing option for handheld gaming enthusiasts.
Boiling Steam speculates that the Steam Deck was an interesting option when it sold for $650 but is a complete waste of money when priced at around $1,000 for the 1TB model. Furthermore, affluent gamers looking for a handheld at that price point will likely gravitate toward more powerful machines, such as the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ or the Asus ROG Ally X.
If the publication's methodology checks out, we might soon see a dramatic collapse in Steam Machine sales as well. The IT industry is currently going through a series of massive transformations, which means it's probably too early to say that the Steam Deck is completely finished. After all, Valve engineers recently confirmed that things can always get worse.

articles.title: Robot snakes searched for Venezuela earthquake survivors in collapsed buildings
articles.text:
Robots slithered like snakes into the rubble of collapsed buildings to search for trapped survivors in the aftermath of Venezuela’s double earthquake disaster.
The so-called snake robots represented a unique technological aid for international search and rescue efforts following two earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24, killing more than 5,000 people and leaving behind 16,740 injured. Rescuers from around the world used trained dogs, seismic and acoustic listening devices, video cameras on sticks, or thermal imaging cameras to search for signs of survivors—but the snakebots equipped with a video camera could squeeze through tight spaces to search deep within fallen building debris.
“The reason why snake robots are useful is they can get into tightly packed volumes that machinery and people otherwise cannot, and that’s important in search and rescue because we were able to extend the visual reach of the rescue workers in a safe way,” Howie Choset, head of the Biorobotics Lab at Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, told Ars. “In a sense, you’re doing minimally invasive surgery on a structure with a snake robot.”
Each 4-foot-long snakebot is modular in design with individual body segments that can be swapped out and easily replaced or upgraded. A human operator directs the robot using a video game controller and a control case laptop tethered to the robot, but software algorithms allow the robot to autonomously coordinate the body segments for the appropriate body movements when being directed to travel from point A to B.
Choset and his colleagues have spent nearly two decades developing different versions of the snake robots that can explore archaeological sites, swim underwater and even assist with minimally invasive surgery. But they first put the snake robot to the test in search and rescue scenarios following an earthquake that struck Mexico City on September 19, 2017, when they helped search a collapsed apartment building.

articles.title: 'The Rings of Power' season 3 trailer launch live — all of the build-up to the release of the Amazon Prime Video TV show's next teaser
articles.text:
The Rings of Power season 3 trailer launch live — all of the latest news and rumors on the next teaser for Amazon's The Lords of the Rings TV show
The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power season 3 will make its Prime Video debut this November
Get ready, The Lord of the Rings fans, because the first trailer for The Rings of Power season 3 is almost here.
Set to be released today (Friday, July 26) following its premiere at San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) 2026, the teaser will give us our first proper look at the Amazon TV Original's next season, which is set to make its Prime Video debut in mid-November.
So, grab some Lembas bread and join TechRadar's senior entertainment reporter Tom Power as he counts down towards the trailer's grand reveal. The Dark Lord Sauron demands it...
Nine for mortal men, doomed to die...
As for the other confirmed character, Zubin Varla is set to portray Khamûl the Easterling. That's one of the nine Kings of Men who are gifted a Ring of Power by Sauron and who — spoilers — end up becoming his chief lieutenants, aka the Nazgûl, aka the Ringwraiths.
Chatting to Empire, Varla said this nontuplet "go on the same journey as Gollum" — i.e., we'll see them slowly get warped by the dark magic within the rings they're handed. In the same article, McKay also revealed that they won't be known as the Nazgûl just yet, either. Instead, they'll be referred to as the Nazgnagôl, or "ring-servants". Think of them as proto-Ringwraiths, basically.
The Lord of Lothlórien
Of the aforementioned reveals, here's one that'll come as a relief to fans.
Ever since The Rings of Power began, viewers have wondered why Celeborn hasn't been part of proceedings. Indeed, apart from him briefly being mentioned in season 1 by his paramour Galadriel, Celeborn has been surprisingly conspicuous by his absence.
Thankfully, he'll be an active participant in season 3. Per Empire, Campbell-Bower will feature as the Elf lord and warrior, who's described as something of a "lover boy" by the actor himself. It's unclear how much of Celeborn we'll see but, hey, whether it's via flashback sequences or in the present, it's high time that he showed up.
New season, new faces
Leaping ahead years into the future isn't necessarily a bad thing. In fact, one positive it can have is allowing for the introduction of characters we wouldn't otherwise see until much later in the story.
We've already received confirmation of five new names who've joined next season's cast, too. Last February, Stranger Things alumnus Jamie Campbell-Bower and Heartstopper's Eddie Marsan were added to The Rings of Power 3's ensemble. Four months later, three fresh faces in Andrew Richardson, Zubin Varla, and Adam Young also joined The Rings of Power season 3.
At the time of their hirings, Amazon declined to say who they'd be playing. Thanks to Empire's recent cover feature, though, we now know the identity of Campbell-Bower and Varla's individuals...
Time jump!
So, why we won't see the War of the Elves and Sauron from the very beginning? Because season 3 takes a giant leap forward in time.
Per this season's official story synopsis, it'll jump forward "several years from the events of season 2" and "takes place at the height of The War of the Elves and Sauron, as the Dark Lord seeks to craft the One Ring that will give him the edge he needs to win the war and all of Middle-earth at last."
What does that mean for what we'll actually see? Hopefully, season 3 will dispense with any mundane parts of the conflict and depict its most exciting albeit deadly encounters, including the Siege of Rivendell and pivotal Battle of Gwathló.
The Last Homely House East of the Sea
Sauron's desire to make the titular, all-powerful, and manipulative piece of jewelry will stem from those who continue to resist his aim to achieve world domination.
Indeed, last season's finale all but confirmed that its follow-up would depict the War of the Elves and Sauron, aka one of the longest-running and bloodiest conflicts of Middle-earth's Second Age. And, while we won't see how this war plays out from the get-go — more on why shortly — we're bound to witness the rise of Rivendell.
Season 3 isn't the first time we've seen the famous Elven city, mind you — or, at the very least, that land upon which it'll be built. Towards the end of season 2 episode 8, the elves who fled Eregion's destruction regrouped at an area that, thanks to its nearby waterfall, would be very familiar to Lord of the Rings diehards. That being, Imladris, otherwise known as Rivendell.
In an exclusive chat with TechRadar in October 2024, Robert Aramayo and Benjamin Walker, who portray Elrond and Gil-galad, refused to confirm if last season's finale represented the founding of Rivendell. However, Walker admitted it was a "very astute observation" on my part, so I took that as confirmation without him actually confirming it.
Regardless, if we don't see Rivendell's formation and/or it being used as a base of operations for the elven crusade against Sauron this season, I'll eat my hat (NB: I won't actually, but you don't know that...).
Forging the One Ring
One thing that's been clear since last season ended was that the show's next installment would finally show us how the One Ring was forged.
Speaking exclusively to TechRadar in October 2024, Charlie Vickers, who plays Sauron, said the One Ring's creation was "the next piece of the puzzle" where The Lord of the Rings franchise's infamous villain was concerned.
At the time, Vickers had no idea if he'd get to forge it in the fires of Mount Doom in season 3. However, in a recent cover piece for Empire magazine, Vickers and the show's co-creators J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay confirmed season 3 would include one of the most significant moments in Middle-earth history.
Per Vickers, it took two weeks to shoot the entirety of the Ring's creation, with McKay also saying it was "the single most ambitious, technically challenging sequence we’ve ever done on the show". Big words, indeed — let's hope the pay-off is worth it!
I return to you, at the turn of the tide!
Alright, I've had my fill of food, stayed away from half pints and pints — hey, I'm still on the clock! — and ready to power through for the next five to six hours.
So, where were we...
Lunch break!
Curses, I've missed Elevenses... guess I'll just have to go straight to luncheon! Now, should I have 'taters? And should I boil 'em, mash 'em, or stick 'em in a stew...
What do we know so far about The Rings of Power season 3?
I'm glad you asked, dear reader — and, just like this blog's last post, I've got a handy guide all things season 3-related for you to check out at your leisure.
So, if you want the lowdown on the biggest and latest news and rumors about the show's next outing, find out everything we know so far about The Rings of Power season 3.
About last season's finale...
Excited though I am — and, hopefully, you are — for this season's arrival, it has been almost two years since The Rings of Power season 2 ended.
Given the myriad shows we've all likely consumed in the months since, I wouldn't be surprised if you've forgotten what happened last time around. Good job there's an article of mine that explains The Rings of Power season 2's ending and how it sets up its sequel season, then, isn't it!
Ringin' in the release date
We might not have a trailer — yet — for season 3, but we do have an official launch date: November 11, 2026. Amazon confirmed The Rings of Power season 3's late 2026 arrival in mid-May, so we've been counting down the days to its return for over two months at this point.
And, honestly? I'm glad it'll be here before the end of the year. Filming only wrapped on The Rings of Power 3 in December 2025 and, given how the lengthy cycle of its predecessors' post-production stages, I fully expected the forthcoming season's post-production phase to not only be similarly long, but also mean it wouldn't arrive until early 2027. Thank God I was wrong!
When will The Rings of Power season 3 trailer be released?
Let's get the big question out of the way first: what time should we expect this season's first trailer to drop?
Well, we know it'll be sometime today — aka Friday, July 26 — but its actual launch time hasn't been announced.
That said, an Amazon MGM Studios SDCC 2026 presentation will tell us more about The Rings of Power 3 and another of its forthcoming TV shows in Blade Runner 2099. That panel kicks off at 10am PT / 1pm ET / 6pm BST, and is expected to last for 90 minutes, so the trailer will be with us by 11:30am PT / 2:30pm ET / 7:30pm BST at the very latest.
In the first of Mount Doom...
Hello and welcome to our The Rings of Power season 3 trailer live blog. I'm Tom Power, TechRadar's senior entertainment reporter and master of ceremonies for today's teaser unveiling.
We're still many hours away from the video's world premiere, but there's plenty for us to chat about in the meantime. So, join me, won't you, as we count down to our first look at the high fantasy show's next season.

articles.title: Hybridflugzeug der NASA bricht einen Höhenrekord
articles.text:
Die NASA und der US-Triebwerkshersteller GE Aerospace haben ein Regionalflugzeug mit Hybridantrieb auf 9.100 Meter Höhe gebracht. Das entspricht der üblichen Reiseflughöhe von 30.000 Fuß – und ist ein Meilenstein. Denn erstmals erreicht ein hybrid-elektrisches Flugzeug den Bereich von Verkehrsmaschinen.
Die Maschine vom Typ Saab 340B wurde von der Weltraumbehörde in Zusammenarbeit mit GE Aerospace umgerüstet. Wann der Rekordflug stattfand, wurde nicht verraten. Klar ist aber, dass die Maschine von der Öffentlichkeit begutachten werden kann: Auf der aktuell laufenden Farnborough International Air Show, die am 28. Juli bei London zu Ende geht.
Regionaljet mit 37 Sitzplätzen als Testträger
Das Testfahrzeug wurde nicht zufällig ausgewählt: Das Regionalflugzeug bietet Platz für 33 bis 37 Passagiere, dient also etwa der Anbindung kleinerer Flughäfen und für Zubringdienste. Saab und Fairchild entwickelten es einst gemeinsam, die Produktion lief von 1984 bis 2005. Normalerweise treiben zwei Turboprop-Triebwerke die Maschine an, also Gasturbinen, die ihre Leistung über einen Propeller abgeben.
Die GE- und NASA-Ingenieure ersetzten eines der beiden Triebwerke nun durch einen Hybridantrieb. Dieser besteht aus drei Komponenten: einer Gasturbine, einem Elektromotor und einem Energiespeicher. Die Gasturbine erzeugt Strom. Dieser speist den Elektromotor und lädt gleichzeitig den Akku. Dabei werden Leistungen im Megawattbereich erzielt.
Weniger Treibstoff ohne Leistungsverlust
Das Projekt startete 2021. Neben NASA und GE Aerospace beteiligten sich die Luftfahrtunternehmen Boeing und BetaTechnologies daran. Die NASA will nach eigenen Angaben zeigen, dass ein Hybridantrieb mindestens leistungsfähig genug für ein Flugzeug in der Größe eines Regionaljets ist. Das Ziel: Treibstoffverbrauch und Kosten senken, keine Leistungseinbußen.
Die NASA erwartet, dass die Technik und das Design des Antriebs bei der Entwicklung künftiger kommerzieller Flugzeug-Hybridsysteme helfen werden. Diese könnten die Betriebskosten von Fluggesellschaften deutlich reduzieren und eine Zwischenstufe bis zu reinen Elektroantrieben bieten.

articles.title: Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 to be held from Nov 17-19
articles.text:
Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 to be held from Nov 17-19
BTS 2026 is expected to bring together more than 1,800 exhibitors, 25,000 delegates, 1,000 tech startups, and over 60,000 business visitors from 75 countries and 30 States & Union Territories of India.
The Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS), the flagship event of the Government of Karnataka showcasing the State's technological prowess, will be held in Bengaluru from November 17 to 19, with a special focus on startups, the semiconductor industry, and sustainability.
The theme of this year's summit is "AI & Beyond." BTS 2026 is expected to bring together more than 1,800 exhibitors, 25,000 delegates, 1,000 technology startups, and over 60,000 business visitors from 75 countries and 30 States and Union Territories across India.
A key highlight of the summit will be the Future Makers programme, designed to spotlight high-potential startups and connect them with investors, mentors, and global markets. The programme will feature investor pitch sessions, one-on-one mentoring clinics, thematic discussions on scaling and fundraising, a Startup Showcase, and the Future Makers Conclave.
BTS 2026 will also host the inaugural edition of embedded world India, featuring a dedicated conference track and exhibition pavilion focused on electronics and semiconductors.
Another co-located event at BTS 2026 is the India edition of ChangeNOW, which focuses on environmental and social solutions for the planet.
The State government also hosted its annual CEO Breakfast Meet in Bengaluru on Friday, bringing together more than 200 technology industry leaders, including the State's leading entrepreneurs, industry executives, investors, and policymakers, for a high-level dialogue on advancing Karnataka's innovation and technology agenda.
The meeting was attended by Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and IT Minister Priyank Kharge.
Kharge said, "One of Karnataka's greatest strengths has been the trust and partnership we have built with industry. The CEO Breakfast Meet embodies that relationship, bringing together government and industry not only to exchange ideas, but to jointly shape the State's technology agenda.”
He further added, “As we announce Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, we reaffirm our vision of building a globally connected innovation ecosystem that drives technological leadership, entrepreneurship and inclusive growth."
The CEO breakfast meet also marked the launch of the Innoverse Foundation, an initiative of the Government of Karnataka aimed at positioning the State as a global deeptech capital. The foundation will act as a catalyst by mentoring successful, revenue-generating deeptech startups, helping them evolve from achieving strong product-market fit to becoming industry leaders.
Edited by Megha Reddy

articles.title: Votre vieux Google Home Mini gagne une seconde vie grâce à Gemini Live
articles.text:
Si vous avez une ancienne enceinte connectée ou une caméra connectée de Google, vous serez ravi d’apprendre que vous n’aurez pas à en racheter un modèle plus récent pour profiter de Gemini Live, le mode d’échange vocal naturel de l’IA de Google. L’entreprise vient en effet d’annoncer l’arrivée de certaines nouveautés jusque là réservées aux derniers modèles sur certains « anciens » appareils Google Home.
Gemini Live débarque sur les Google Home Mini et anciens Nest Hub
Inauguré d’abord sur la gamme récente (Nest Mini, Nest Audio, Nest Hub Max et Nest Hub), l’assistant Gemini Live débarque enfin sur les Google Home Mini et Google Nest Hub de première génération. La mise à jour reste cependant réservée aux abonnés Google Home Premium. Pour l’activer, il faut passer par le traditionnel « Hey Google » avant d’engager la conversation.
Google en a également profité pour étendre la fenêtre de mémoire de Gemini for Home à 15 minutes. Concrètement, vous allez par exemple pouvoir demander l’allumage des lumières de la cuisine, puis ajuster leur intensité à 50 % plusieurs minutes plus tard (moins de 15 minutes après donc) sans devoir répéter le contexte de votre requête. Pratique.
Des correctifs sur mobile et une surveillance supplémentaire pour le chauffage
L’application Google Home profite également de ce déploiement pour corriger plusieurs bugs gênants sur smartphone : la jauge de batterie des caméras sera désormais plus précise et la diffusion du flux vidéo en direct devient aussi plus fluide sur l’application iOS.
À lire : Gemini Live règle enfin le plus gros défaut de son interface
Côté matériel, les propriétaires de thermostats Nest profitent aussi désormais d’une alerte de santé système automatisée, c’est-à-dire que l’appareil est capable d’identifier préventivement les dysfonctionnements du compresseur de votre climatisation ou de votre pompe à chaleur. articles.title: SAP shrugs off fears of AI eating software with big earnings beat - SiliconANGLE

SAP shrugs off fears of AI eating software with big earnings beat
Enterprise software giant SAP SE’s stock inched up in late trading today after it shook off concerns that its business might become a victim of the artificial intelligence boom by posting solid results in its latest earnings report.
The strong numbers posted by SAP today suggest that AI tools that can automate some kinds of business work and processes aren’t yet replacing its software, which spans cloud services and operating systems for large enterprises.
The company reported second-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of €1.89 ($2.15) per share, surpassing Wall Street’s consensus estimate of €1.68 by a wide margin. Meanwhile, SAP’s revenue increased 11% from the same period one year ago, to €9.88 billion, beating the €9.85 billion analyst target.
Those numbers helped SAP post an operating profit of €4.16 billion in the quarter, up from a profit of just €3.54 billion one year ago. Investors liked what they saw, and SAP’s American depository receipts gained more than 2% in the after-hours trading session.
SAP’s cloud business unit, which is by far its largest segment, saw sales grow 24% from a year earlier. Meanwhile, its cloud backlog jumped 26% to €22.9 billion, the company said. The business has grown immensely in recent years as more of SAP’s customers shift their data from on-premises database systems to SAP’s cloud platform, which generates a recurring source of revenue. However, that shift has come at the expense of the company’s software support revenue, which declined 7% in the quarter.
Like many software companies, SAP has been under pressure for the last year amid fears that AI tools will one day, perhaps even soon, replace the need for traditional software tools. After all, why pay to use an expensive enterprise resource planning platform when you can simply have an AI coding bot create one for you for free? Fortunately for SAP, doing that isn’t nearly as simple as it seems. However, its stock has still declined 40% in the year to date, primarily on those concerns.
But SAP is trying to change the narrative, and its management insists that it can actually become one of the leading AI providers. Chief Executive Christian Klein (pictured) argued that generic AI tools simply cannot match the capabilities and reliability of SAP’s embedded AI solutions.
“Customers are choosing SAP to enable accurate and compliant AI outcomes grounded in their most critical business processes and data,” he insisted.“We delivered another quarter of strong current cloud backlog growth, up 26% at constant currencies. This performance is underpinned by our Autonomous Enterprise strategy with strong momentum across our Autonomous Suite as well as our Business AI Platform.”
SAP did not bump up its revenue guidance, instead just reiterating an earlier forecast for its full-year revenue and cash flow. However, it did reduce its guidance for non-adjusted operating profit by €100 million, following its acquisitions of Dremio Inc. and Prior Labs GmbH in May.

articles.title: Por qué todos están preguntando en Google si el pollo se compra con piel amarilla o blanca: la tendencia inesperada
articles.text:
En Google se ha hecho tendencia la búsqueda de las diferencias entre el pollo de piel amarilla y piel blanca, ya que suelen ser opciones que normalmente están en las tiendas y no está claro cuál es de mejor calidad, sabor o métodos de preparación.
Según entidades, como la Federación Avícola Catalana, las diferencias entre ambos tipos no solo se reducen a la apariencia, sino que están directamente relacionadas con la alimentación del ave y el método de crianza, aspectos que también influyen en la textura y el gusto de la carne.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuáles son las diferencias entre el pollo de piel amarilla y piel blanca
- El origen del color
El color de la piel del pollo se determina principalmente por los ingredientes presentes en su dieta. Los pollos con piel amarilla suelen alimentarse con productos ricos en carotenoides, compuestos naturales que se encuentran en alimentos como el maíz amarillo, la alfalfa y ciertos tipos de flores.
Estos pigmentos se depositan en la grasa subcutánea, otorgando ese característico tono dorado a la piel y, en ocasiones, incluso a la carne y la grasa.
PUBLICIDAD
En contraste, los pollos de piel blanca reciben una alimentación basada en cereales como el trigo o el sorgo, que contienen una cantidad mucho menor de carotenoides. Al no acumular estos pigmentos, la piel conserva un color más claro y la carne suele resultar más tierna y de sabor suave.
La Federación Avícola Catalana señala que “los pollos de crecimiento lento que encontramos en el mercado, tanto los camperos como otros tipos, suelen ser de color amarillo debido a las preferencias de los consumidores, quienes asociamos este color con una mayor rusticidad y con la cría al aire libre”.
PUBLICIDAD
- Valor nutricional y calidad de la carne
Una de las preguntas más frecuentes es si existe una diferencia nutricional real entre el pollo de piel amarilla y el de piel blanca. El color de la piel no determina la calidad ni el valor nutricional del producto. Ambos tipos de carne ofrecen proteínas de alta calidad, vitaminas del complejo B y minerales como fósforo y selenio en proporciones similares.
La carne de pollo, en general, es magra, con bajo contenido en grasa, especialmente cuando se consume sin piel.
El aporte de vitaminas y minerales se mantiene estable independientemente de la dieta del animal. La única variación significativa es la presencia de carotenoides en los pollos de piel amarilla, compuestos que actúan como antioxidantes, aunque esta diferencia es mínima y no modifica sustancialmente los beneficios nutricionales para el consumidor.
PUBLICIDAD
- Sabor, textura y usos en la cocina
El color de la piel también influye en la experiencia culinaria y en las preparaciones recomendadas. El pollo de piel amarilla, por su alimentación y, en ocasiones, por una crianza de crecimiento más lento, suele tener una textura más firme y un sabor percibido como más intenso.
Esta variedad es muy apreciada en países de Europa y América Latina para recetas al horno o a la parrilla, donde el aspecto dorado resulta atractivo y la piel crujiente suma valor al plato.
PUBLICIDAD
Por su parte, el pollo de piel blanca se distingue por una carne más tierna y un gusto más suave. Es ideal para preparaciones donde se busca una textura delicada, como guisos, platos cocidos, frituras o ensaladas. Su versatilidad lo convierte en una opción popular para quienes priorizan la suavidad en la carne y la facilidad de digestión.
La elección entre uno y otro depende, en gran medida, de las preferencias personales y del tipo de plato que se pretenda preparar. Quienes buscan una presentación dorada y un sabor más pronunciado suelen optar por el pollo de piel amarilla, mientras que aquellos que priorizan la ternura y la neutralidad en el gusto prefieren la piel blanca.
PUBLICIDAD
La elección entre pollo de piel amarilla o blanca no debe basarse únicamente en el color de la piel, sino en otros factores que garantizan la calidad y frescura del producto. Se recomienda que la carne presente un aspecto firme y uniforme, sin olores desagradables.
La piel debe estar íntegra y libre de manchas verdosas o grisáceas. El pollo debe mantenerse siempre refrigerado y respetar la fecha de vencimiento indicada.

articles.title: Keychron Launches BM27 Affordable Silent Wireless Ergonomic Mouse
articles.text:
Thursday, July 23rd 2026
	
	
	
	Keychron Launches BM27 Affordable Silent Wireless Ergonomic Mouse
Keychron's latest mouse deviates from the brand's recent focus on gaming peripherals and throws a bone to office workers with a penchant for comfort. The BM27 is a wireless ergonomic mouse with a 55° angled grip and silent micro switches on all buttons. The BM27 has six programmable buttons including the left, right, and middle click buttons. In other words, there are three additional programmable buttons that can be customized in Keychron Launcher: one behind the scroll wheel and two thumb keys on the side. 
The BM27 is built around the PixArt PAW 3212 sensor, which delivers up to 2400 DPI resolution and tracking at speeds up to 30 IPS, and the polling maxes out at 1 kHz. While this performance is ample for the intended productivity use cases, it's likely insufficient for gaming. It has both Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz wireless connectivity, as well as wired USB Type-C connectivity, and the 500 mAh battery promises up to 100 hours of usage over Bluetooth. The BM27 is relatively affordable, at $34.99 on Keychron's online store. It is only available in Space Gray at the time of writing, and it has a soft-touch UV finish on for additional comfort.The Keychron BM27 comes with both a USB Type-C and Type-A dongle for 2.4 GHz connectivity, making it usable with both desktop PCs and modern port-starved laptops and even tablets, and it has a dedicated storage compartment for the Type-A dongle in the bottom of the mouse. The BM27 measures in at 66.57 (H) × 111.61 (L) × 83.91 (W) mm and weighs in at a relatively hefty 99 g.

Am Anfang stand eine Mitarbeiterbefragung vor acht Jahren: „Die Ergebnisse haben uns aufhorchen lassen“, sagt der heutige Klinik-Controller Norman Daßler von der bayerischen Klinik Wartenberg. Denn die Mitarbeitenden der Klinik hatten mit Schlafproblemen zu tun, die sie stark belasteten: „Unsere Angestellten hatten durch Schlafprobleme mit Ermüdungszuständen, Kopfschmerzen und Herz-Kreislauf-Problemen zu kämpfen.“, so Daßler, der zum Zeitpunkt der Umfrage noch als Pflegedienstleiter tätig war. Ungefähr zeitgleich kam auch die jährliche Auswertung der Arbeitsunfähigkeitsmeldungen der AOK Bayern, der Krankenkasse, bei der über die Hälfte der Angestellten versichert sind. Diese bestätigte die Ergebnisse der Umfrage noch einmal.

articles.title: AMD’s 256-core Epyc 9996 ‘Venice’ claims up to a 3.4x jump over Intel Xeon competition, 20% over Nvidia Vera – Zen 6 comes with up to 1024MB of L3, 16-channel memory, and 5GHz+ clock speeds
articles.text:
AMD’s 256-core Epyc 9996 ‘Venice’ claims up to a 3.4x jump over Intel Xeon competition, 20% over Nvidia Vera – Zen 6 comes with up to 1024MB of L3, 16-channel memory, and 5GHz+ clock speeds
That’s a big chip.
AMD is finally providing some details on its first Zen 6 CPU, which it has been teasing for over a year. The Epyc 9996 is a 256-core / 512-thread chip, packing AMD’s new Zen 6 architecture, and it’s the first to launch in what AMD describes as a “broad portfolio” for Venice. In addition to claiming significant performance advantages over the impending Nvidia Vera and Intel’s Xeon 6, AMD says it will continue to build out the Venice range with bespoke designs over the next year.
“It’s not just a single processor,” said AMD’s Ravi Kuppuswany, corporate VP of compute and enterprise solutions.q “It’s a portfolio.” AMD says it has purpose-built solutions, splitting its offerings depending on the application, not dissimilar to how Intel has split its Xeon ranges over the past few generations (nor how AMD has softly segmented its Epyc offerings). The roadmap starts with the main Venice lineup on the SP7 socket, which is what AMD has been teasing for so long. It scales up to 256 cores and 512 threads, 1.6 TB/s of memory bandwidth with fast MRDIMMs, and 128 PCIe 6 lanes in 1P configuration (160 lanes in 2P).
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Note: When scaling up to 256 cores, AMD uses its Zen 6c “dense” design. With a standard Zen 6 design, AMD says Venice scales up to 128 cores and 256 threads, while high-frequency variations top out at 96 cores.
In the first half of next year, AMD plans to launch Venice on its SP8 socket, offering as few as eight cores and up to 128, focused on smaller deployments. These chips support eight-channel memory with two DIMMs per channel, and the same 128 PCIe 6 lanes.
Venice-X is expected in the second half of 2027, on the SP7 socket. We didn’t see Turin-X, but the last, last-gen Genoa-X came with 96 cores and up to 1152 MB of stacked L3 cache. Those specs haven’t changed (short of the Zen 6 microarchitecture), but AMD says it's able to clock Venice-X up to 5.15 GHz.
Finally, Verano should arrive in the second half of next year on the SP8 socket, and it looks like the most direct competitor to Vera (AMD’s Kuppuswamy had some fun with calling it “Vera-No”). It’s optimized to be an AI host node, says AMD, packing up to 72 cores and 5 GHz peak clocks. Critically, it comes with a 24-channel LPDDR5X memory system, leveraging SOCAMM2 modules.
| Chip | Cores / Threads | Base / Boost Clock (GHz) | L3 Cache | TDP | 
| Epyc 9996 | 256 / 512 | 2.55 / 4.1 | 1024 MB | 600W | 
| Epyc 9966 | 192 / 384 | 2.9 / 4 | 768 MB | 600W | 
| Epyc 9846 | 168 / 336 | 2.85 / 3.7 | 768 MB | 500W | 
| Epyc 9756 | 128 / 256 | 3.15 / 4 | 512 MB | 500W | 
| Epyc 9G76 | 96 / 192 | 3.4 / 4.8 | 384 MB | 500W | 
| Epyc 9656 | 96 / 192 | 3.05 / 3.7 | 512 MB | 400W | 
| Epyc 9686F | 96 / 192 | 3.4 / 5 | 384 MB | 500W | 
| Epyc 9556 | 64 / 128 | 2.75 / 4.3 | 384 MB | 300W | 
| Epyc 9586F | 64 / 128 | 3.75 / 5 | 384 MB | 500W | 
One of the advantages Nvidia claims with its Vera chip is lots of memory bandwidth through the LPDDR5X system. AMD’s approach is different with Venice SP7. It’s scaling up to 16-channel memory with Venice SP7, with support for MRDIMMs running at 12,800 MT/s, or standard DDR5 RDIMMs running at 8000 MT/s.

It’s a significant jump over Turin, which uses 12-channel memory, with support for RDIMMs running at 6400 MT/s. AMD claims per-socket bandwidth of 1.6 TB/s, significantly higher than the 1.2 TB/s available on Vera, and nearly triple the 576 GB/s per-socket bandwidth of Turin. Intel recently enabled 8000 MT/s RDIMMs on select Granite Rapids and Clearwater Forest SKUs, and it says support for MRDIMMs with speeds up to 8800 MT/s is coming in Q1 2027.

Zen 6 is built on TSMC’s N2 (this has been previously confirmed). AMD confirmed that there are 32 cores on a CCD, along with two IODs. Keep in mind that the 32-core CCD is using Zen 6c, not full Zen 6. There has been plenty of speculation about 32-core CCDs in consumer Zen 6 CPUs, but that seems unlikely.
The 256-core configuration comes with a massive 1,024 MB of L3, nearly triple the amount of the Epyc 9965. This isn’t stacked cache, either; that will come with Venice-X. Each CCD has access to 128 MB or L3, or 4 MB per core, double what was available on Turin.
Although AMD has focused a lot of its teases on the 256-core Venice, the initial SP7 offerings will also hold a 96-core, high-frequency model that can clock up to 5 GHz.
AMD shares first 256-core Epyc ‘Venice’ benchmarks

Unlike the extrapolated performance AMD shared a few weeks back, we have some concrete benchmarks for the Epyc 9996 now. AMD has, unsurprisingly, focused the workloads around agentic AI. However, many of the workloads applicable for agentic AI are applicable elsewhere, as well, including high-concurrency networking tasks, code compilation, and media processing.
Note that AMD includes just the Epyc 9965 as a gen-on-gen comparison point in the charts above. This is a “dense” Zen 5 design with 192 cores. Results for the 128-core 9755 are included in the tables below.
Starting with front-end operations, AMD claims a 1.2x gen-on-gen improvement and a 2.8x improvement compared to Intel Xeon 6980P, with an NGINX web server using the WRK load generator. Unlike most of these competitive performance figures, AMD included the actual numbers for the benchmarks it ran in the footnotes, which you can see in the table below.
| Chip | Max Request Per Second | 
| Intel Xeon 6980P | 10,162,179 | 
| AWS Graviton5 | 15,331,108 | 
| AMD Epyc 9755 | 17,906,196 | 
| AMD Epyc 9965 | 24,320,476 | 
| AMD Epyc 9996 | 28,789,170 | 
In data-heavy workloads that are common among AI agents, AMD claims a 1.7x improvement over Turn, and a massive 3.4x over the Xeon 6980P. AMD used the TPCx-AI benchmark to gather these results. The primary metric for this test is AI use cases per minute (AIUCpm), for which AMD shared the median result2. If you’re interested in more about the reporting of this benchmark, Dell has published an extensive breakdown.
| Chip | AIUCpm | 
| Intel Xeon 6980P | 1,750.36 | 
| AWS Graviton5 | 2,444.8 | 
| AMD Epyc 9755 | 2,704.19 | 
| AMD Epyc 9965 | 3,458.79 | 
| AMD Epyc 9996 | 5,982.91 | 
In vectorized workloads, AMD claims a 1.6x gen-on-gen improvement and 2.3x improvement compared to the Xeon 6980P. For this test, AMD used Meta’s open-source FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) library to search for similar vectors in the siftm1 dataset. The metric here is QPS, or queries processed per second, looking at overall query throughput.
| Chip | QPS | 
| Intel Xeon 6980P | 316,069 | 
| AWS Graviton5 | 119,179 | 
| AMD Epyc 9755 | 369,252 | 
| AMD Epyc 9965 | 472,079 | 
| AMD Epyc 9996 | 751,453 | 
For its “enterprise tools” benchmarks, AMD ran several tests, including TPC-H, TPC-C, and Redis, and it reports the results as “geomean throughput.” We have actual numbers here, but they’re a geomean representing several different tests rather than a single benchmark. Broadly, however, AMD claims a 1.6x gen-on-gen improvement in these workloads, and a 2.6x improvement compared to Intel.
| Chip | Geomean throughput | 
| Intel Xeon 6980P | 2,284,701 | 
| AWS Graviton5 | 2,982,203 | 
| AMD Epyc 9755 | 2,546,290 | 
| AMD Epyc 9965 | 3,867,149 | 
| AMD Epyc 9996 | 6,054,748 | 
A lot of agentic workloads are applicable outside of agents, but AMD also tested a few agents directly. It replayed five different agent personas across the chips and, once again, gathered a throughput geomean. We don’t have the metrics here, nor for the previous benchmark, so it’s possible there’s an angle of performance that we’re not seeing with the data provided by AMD.
Regardless, the company claims a 1.5x gen-on-gen improvement in this test, and a 2.5x improvement compared to the 6980P.
| Chip | Geomean throughput | 
| Intel Xeon 6980P | 1.779 | 
| AWS Graviton5 | 2.505 | 
| AMD Epyc 9755 | 2.317 | 
| AMD Epyc 9965 | 2.97 | 
| AMD Epyc 9996 | 4.451 | 
AMD ran these tests earlier in the month. But just a few days ago, Nvidia published its first SPEC CPU 2026 results for Vera. AMD ran some tests of its own using the same compiler for a comparison between Vera and Venice. AMD’s Kuppuswamy says, “everything is apples-to-apples comparison, same compiler.” That’s GNU 15.2, if you’re curious.
In throughput, AMD claims a 2.2x improvement in the SPECrate integer suite, compared to Vera using the dense Venice design with 256 Zen 6c cores. More importantly, AMD claims a 1.2x improvement in per-core performance when comparing Vera to a 96-core “High Frequency” Venice chip. AMD says it used Nvidia’s results as the basis for comparison. With both Venice designs, AMD used a 600W TDP.
In SPEC CPU 2017 (again using SPECrate with integer workloads), AMD has data comparing Venice to Intel’s 6980P and Arm’s new AGI, showing 2x throughput compared to Intel, and 1.3x per-core performance. Note the core counts here for AMD. SPECrate is a throughput test, and AMD stepping down to a 128-core model suggests that performance will likely drop off as the core count increases.
Although AMD wants to focus Venice performance on agentic workloads, it shared a range of what are now being called “legacy” workloads across the cloud and HPC. Some of the results are repeated from the earlier slides, such as Redis and NGINX, but there are some additional data points, including NAMD and SQL. The performance improvements here are large, though not surprising. You can see that across these tests, even Turin beats the competition from Intel and AWS.

Jake Roach is the Senior CPU Analyst at Tom’s Hardware, writing reviews, news, and features about the latest consumer and workstation processors.

articles.title: OpenAI's new voice mode makes it to the ChatGPT desktop app | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI on Thursday said it has updated its ChatGPT desktop app to add support for ChatGPT Voice, allowing users to talk to the app to control AI agents and perform tasks on their computer.
The new feature taps OpenAI’s new family of voice models called ChatGPT-Live, which it launched earlier this month.
OpenAI said ChatGPT Voice works with both ChatGPT Work and Codex, and can also tap computer use skills to look up websites and apps. Plus, on macOS, with Appshots, users can let the app access what’s on their screen, including alt-text.
At launch, ChatGPT Voice’s smartphone version featured smoother conversations, with better interruption handling, but it was not built to take action on smartphones.
Thursday’s desktop update is more capable, allowing users to dictate complex commands involving many steps, and respond when ChatGPT needs their input.
In a demo video, OpenAI showed a developer asking ChatGPT to create a new thread, make a pull request, and find the root cause for a bug, with one command.
The company said that users can utilize ChatGPT Voice in Codex from the iOS app through remote access.
Anthropic has also updated its voice mode for Claude, which can tap the company’s Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models to complete tasks in apps like Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion, and Canva.

articles.title: Alphabet (Google) annonce de superbes résultats... son cours à la Bourse chute brutalement. L'IA ne fait plus rêver ?
articles.text:
Les bons résultats financiers ne sont pas toujours automatiquement récompensés à la Bourse. C'est le cas aujourd'hui d'Alphabet.
Depuis l'explosion de la technologie de l'intelligence artificielle, on ne cesse de voir des montants fous s'afficher à la Bourse, jusqu'à l'entrée en Bourse la plus importante de l'histoire avec SpaceX. Mais la folie pourrait commencer à sérieusement se calmer, vu les réactions du marché à ce qui a pourtant été un très bon trimestre 2026 pour Google.
Alphabet surpasse les attentes des analystes, son cours recule fortement à la Bourse
Alphabet (Google) a fait très bien lors du deuxième trimestre 2026, en annonçant des résultats supérieurs aux attentes des analystes. Son chiffre d'affaires se monte ainsi à 119,8 milliards de dollars, soit tout simplement une croissance de 24% sur un an - et une série de douze trimestres consécutifs en croissance à deux chiffres.
Autant dire qu'avec un tel niveau de croissance, porté par l'explosion des revenus cloud (+82%, à 24,8 milliards d'euros), on pouvait s'attendre à une réaction positive du marché. Et pourtant, le cours à la Bourse d'Alphabet a réculé aujourd'hui de près de 6,5%.
Les investissements IA sur la sellette
Car si, évdemment, Alphabet reste une entreprise très profitabnle, la variable scrutée par les investisseurs est ailleurs. Ils ont en effet observé Alphabet revoir à la hausse ses prévisions d'investissement en 2026, auparavant de 180 à 190 milliards d'euros, et qui sont dorénavant estimées entre 195 et 205 milliards d'euros.
Des dépenses qui montent pour soutenir la course dans l'intelligence artificielle. Or, les investisseurs commencent à se poser des questions sur la rentabilité future de ces investissements gargantuesques. « La réaction instinctive suscitée par les résultats d'Alphabet donne le ton pour les prochaines publications des géants de la tech : les investisseurs s'intéressent de plus en plus au coût croissant des ambitions en matière d'IA plutôt qu'aux résultats supérieurs aux prévisions. Ils ne souhaitent pas davantage de dépenses » a ainsi expliqué Ipek Ozkardeskaya, analyste chez Swissquote. Le début de la fin de l'ivresse ?

articles.title: Comment Google a réduit de moitié les saccades de défilement de Chrome sur Android
articles.text:
Si vous utilisez Google Chrome sur Android, vous avez très certainement vécu cette désagréable expérience de saccade au défilement d’une page Web. Une image qui saute, qui tremble, ou semble se figer l’espace d’un instant et qui donne une impression de manque de fluidité pas franchement confortable.
Ce phénomène, Google l’explique par le fait que pour que tout paraisse fluide, votre smartphone doit afficher une nouvelle image toutes les 16 millisecondes. De ce fait, le moindre retard subi par Chrome génère une saccade.
Google réduit les saccades de 48 % dans Chrome
Pour corriger ce problème de saccade au défilement des pages dans Chrome sur Android, l’équipe en charge du développement a réalisé entre 2023 et 2026 une véritable traque contre ces micro retards et a réussi à les réduire de 48 %.
Pour y arriver, ils se sont penchés sur l’organisation interne de Chrome et ont revu plusieurs éléments de l’architecture du navigateur pour l’optimiser. Concrètement, auparavant, lorsque vous posiez votre doigt sur l’écran de votre smartphone (Input Event), l’information passait par le « cerveau principal » de Chrome. Désormais cette information est directement gérée par le GPU pour décharger le processeur en contournant le thread principal et ainsi éviter un goulot d’étranglement (Input Vizard).
De la même manière, il arrivait que Chrome s’apprête à afficher une image alors que l’information de votre doigt qui touche l’écran arrivait légèrement en retard. Chrome peut désormais patienter un peu pour recevoir l’information et ainsi éviter d’afficher une image qui ne bouge pas (Input Framer).
Par ailleurs, si l’information de votre doigt posé sur l’écran arrive vraiment trop en retard à cause du système, Chrome peut maintenant deviner et prédire (Input Prediction) où votre doigt devrait se trouver en se basant sur vos précédents mouvements, ce qui permet de conserver un mouvement fluide quoi qu’il arrive.
Enfin, l’équipe de développement de Chrome explique avoir supprimé certaines étapes de communication intermédiaires inutiles entre différents composants internes du navigateur, permettant ainsi un précieux gain de temps.

articles.title: Apple's App Store is on pace to add 1 million new apps this year, most are AI slop
articles.text:
The big picture: The number of app submissions to Apple's App Store has risen sharply in 2026, with almost 560,000 new apps reportedly added to the platform between January and June. However, most of these new apps appear to be low-quality offerings, seemingly generated by AI amid a vibecoding trend that is sweeping the developer community.
Data from Sensor Tower suggests that app submissions to the App Store have risen steadily over the past few years, after bottoming out at around 420,000 in 2022. Last year, around 600,000 new apps were listed on the App Store, up 30% from 2024.
The report adds that the number of app submissions has already doubled in the first half of this year, with the momentum expected to continue for the foreseeable future. At the current pace, the App Store is on track to add more than one million new apps in 2026, surpassing its previous record of 890,000 set in 2016.
While the sharp increase in app submissions is a positive development for the global app economy, there is a marked difference in the profile of people submitting apps for approval. The earlier boom was driven entirely by actual developers, whereas the current surge is being driven primarily by people with little or no coding experience.
According to the report, tens of thousands of apps are being created using readily available AI coding tools such as Replit and Bolt.new, which can generate full-stack applications from natural-language prompts. Professional and hobbyist developers are also increasingly using agentic AI tools and assistants, such as Claude Code and GitHub Copilot, to aid them in app development.
Unfortunately for vibe coders, these AI-generated apps are not finding many takers, with App Store downloads reportedly increasing by just 3% last year and 2% so far in 2026. Phillip Shoemaker, who ran the App Store from 2009 to 2016, also recently warned that the surge could strain Apple's resources and allow malicious actors to push malware onto the App Store.
The supply shock is also seemingly delaying the approval process, with complaints on Apple's developer forums suggesting that the time required to approve new apps has increased significantly in recent months. However, Apple has denied those claims, telling The New York Times that it approves 90% of apps within 48 hours.
Copycat apps are also on the rise, with many social media users complaining about low-quality, AI-generated clones that look and function like bad rip-offs of established apps. Recent media reports have also highlighted that many of the new apps on the App Store are either privacy nightmares or simply don't function as advertised.

articles.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming inicia testes de plano gratuito com anúncios • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Xbox Cloud Gaming inicia testes de plano gratuito com anúncios
Xbox Insiders poderão acessar sem custo games selecionados de sua própria biblioteca. Exibição de anúncios dá direito a uma hora de jogo.
Xbox Insiders poderão acessar sem custo games selecionados de sua própria biblioteca. Exibição de anúncios dá direito a uma hora de jogo.
A Microsoft começou os testes para um plano com anúncios do Xbox Cloud Gaming. Inicialmente, o experimento estará disponível para participantes do programa Xbox Insiders, com jogos selecionados que já estejam na biblioteca do usuário.
Por enquanto, não há informações sobre um lançamento oficial do novo plano. A empresa também não divulgou a lista de países e regiões que terão acesso ao teste. O assunto já era especulado há quase um ano, mas agora se tornou mais concreto.
Segundo a Microsoft, esse modelo pode ajudar em países onde os consoles são mais caros ou mais difíceis de encontrar. Assim, quem tem um Xbox One, por exemplo, pode ter acesso a títulos feitos para o Xbox Series S e X sem precisar comprar um novo dispositivo.
A empresa explica que o teste dará direito a uma hora de streaming grátis. As propagandas terão duração de dois minutos e vão aparecer antes da sessão. Quando a hora acabar, o usuário poderá continuar jogando — basta ver mais dois minutos de propagandas.
A experiência com o jogo não sofrerá nenhuma mudança. O acesso é feito com a conta Xbox e estará disponível mesmo que não haja nenhuma assinatura do Xbox Game Pass ativa.
Além disso, a companhia enfatiza que a participação nos testes é opcional e os jogadores podem, a qualquer momento, optar por outras formas de acessar os games.
A empresa divulgou algumas diretrizes sobre as propagandas. Os anúncios devem ter a mesma qualidade do conteúdo para o console, sendo adequados ao que os usuários esperam de cada plataforma. Além disso, as propagandas não devem interromper o jogo. A companhia também se compromete a deixar claro o que é conteúdo publicitário.
“Anúncios existem nos games há décadas, de posicionamentos no próprio jogo a modelos free-to-play. No entanto, eles nem sempre foram feitos tendo em mente o usuário”, diz a Microsoft em seu blog. “Quando feitos da maneira certa, os anúncios podem ajudar a diminuir o custo do acesso.”

articles.title: Microsoft responds to LG monitors installing McAfee ads on Windows
articles.text:
LG is reportedly pulling a McAfee pop-up ad from a controversial app that some of its monitors have stealthily installed on connected computers.
The app, LG Monitor App Installer, installs itself through a Windows Update alongside monitor driver updates. LG Monitor App Installer then pushes ads for a 30-day free trial for McAfee, as well as other software, via a pop-up on affected systems, multiple users have reported.
This has drawn negative attention recently, with complaints surfacing on Reddit and a subsequent video from YouTube channel Gamers Nexus. In the video, editor-in-chief Steve Burke said that the publication paid $1,200 for an LG UltraGear 3GX900A-B gaming monitor (the monitor’s price dropped to $600 two days later, Burke said) for testing and replicated the behavior “several times” across “multiple” Windows 11 systems.
After LG Monitor App Installer was installed, a pop-up appeared on the screen’s lower-right corner “on every single boot,” Burke said. Most of the time, the pop-up was a McAfee ad. The publication also reported seeing ads for LG Switch, LG Calibration Studio, LG Dual Controller, and LG Channels on rare occasions.
McAfee pop-up ad being removed
Following Gamers Nexus’ video, a Microsoft representative stated that the LG Monitor App Installer will no longer show pop-up ads for McAfee. In response to a social media post about the app, Pavan Davuluri, EVP of Windows and devices at Microsoft, said this week:
We’ve connected with the team at LG and as an immediate next step, they have agreed to disable the McAfee pop-up from their app. We appreciate LG working with us toward a shared goal of a better experience for our mutual customers. We will keep improving here with our ecosystem partners.
As mentioned, some LG monitors appear to have been installing LG Monitor App Installer onto Windows computers for months. Publication Windows Latest noted that the app recently got an update, “and its changelog mentions McAfee as an additional app,” which could be what prompted more people to see the ads…and then complain about them.
However, the removal of McAfee doesn’t address the problem of a peripheral installing ad-pushing software onto people’s computers.

articles.title: Stuart Fails to Save the Universe DC crossover has already been quietly teased in trailers — but only this 'iconic' superhero would bring Big Bang Theory lore full circle
articles.text:
Move over, James Gunn: Stuart Fails to Save the Universe will have DC crossover episode — and there's one iconic superhero HBO Max would be stupid not to include
It's literally been staring us in the face for years
I can't say that I've been paying too much attention to what's happening at San Diego Comic Con, but I certainly didn't expect new Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails to Save the Universe and the DC universe to be mentioned in the same breath.
According to Nerdist, DC President Jim Lee made a surprise appearance at the HBO Max show's panel in Hall H, confirming that multiple DC characters will cameo later in the season.
“Some of the DC characters they have in it, I think, are some of the best versions I’ve seen of those characters,” Lee said during the panel.
In other words, watch out James Gunn. With Supergirl failing to make much impact earlier this year, maybe Stuart Fails to Save the Universe actually is the best DC Universe iteration we'll get in 2026.
If you've been watching the teaser trailers closely, you might have seen underrated characters such as Gotham villain Mr. Freeze have already featured. But if creators really want to bring the existing Big Bang Theory lore full circle, the show can't omit the superhero that's been staring us in the face for years.
Stuart Fails to Save the Universe's DC crossover need to include The Flash to commemorate — or spite — Sheldon
Even if you've only watched one episode of Big Bang Theory in your lifetime, my campaign for The Flash to join the Stuart Fails to Save the Universe x DC episode hopefully won't come as a surprise.
He's Sheldon's (Jim Parsons) favorite DC superhero, and the reason why, nearly every time we see him, he's sporting the iconic T-shirt with the Flash logo.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
We're going to be on tenterhooks for all of the new show's 10-episode run to see if Sheldon makes a cameo appearance, and dropping in The Flash as a potential clue could be a really fun way for the creators to mess with us.
On the flip side, a Flash cameo could also work to either spite or celebrate Sheldon. The reason why Stuart (Kevin Sussman) is in this multiverse mess in the first place is because he broke a device built by Sheldon and Leonard (Johnny Galecki); bringing his favorite superhero closer to home could be a great way to apologize.
However, this is a multiverse show, so The Flash likely won't be appearing in the Sheldon we know's reality. So if another Sheldon met the Flash instead... our one would be furious. That, in itself, is hilarious.
At this point, I'm purely speculating. We've got no idea which DC characters will appear in Stuart Fails to Save the Universe, nor do we know exactly which episode they will be in. Regardless, we can definitely assume that the crossover will be an epic one.

articles.title: How OneClickDrive Turned Dubai Used Car Market Into a Marketplace Playbook for India
articles.text:
How OneClickDrive Turned Dubai Used Car Market Into a Marketplace Playbook for India
OneClickDrive's growth in the UAE offers lessons for Indian mobility startups on trust, liquidity, capital efficiency, and building two-sided marketplaces.
India's used car market is still grappling with a fundamental question: should platforms own the vehicles they sell, or simply connect buyers and sellers?
Dubai has already tested both approaches. Over the past decade, its used car market has moved from classified listings, WhatsApp forwards, and weekend meetings in mall parking lots to online marketplaces operating at scale.
OneClickDrive is one of the companies that illustrates that shift.
The UAE and India are very different markets, but the questions facing mobility startups are remarkably similar. OneClickDrive's asset-light marketplace model offers lessons on trust, liquidity and scaling without tying up capital in inventory.
A market built for marketplaces
The UAE was always well suited to a used car marketplace for one simple reason: churn.
A large share of country’s residents are expatriates who typically stay for a few years before moving elsewhere. They arrive, buy a car, and, when it’s time to leave, sell it. This creates a steady supply of well-maintained, GCC-spec vehicles entering the market, resulting in far more turnover per capita than many mature markets.
Depreciation adds to the urgency. A used car in the UAE typically loses 15-20% of its value each year, encouraging sellers to move quickly while buyers compare options rather than remain loyal to a particular dealer. Both sides benefit from anything that reduces friction.
India’s used car market is driven by different factors: a growing middle class, rising demand in metros, and a persistent trust deficit. However, the fundamental are similar: high transaction volumes and an opportunity for platforms that make buying and selling simpler and more reliable. With a large share of Indian expatriate population in the UAE, Indian founders also have a front-row view of how the Gulf model performs in practice.
The real choice: own the car or own the connection?
Every used car platform eventually arrives at the same strategic decision.
The asset-heavy model involves buying vehicles, refurbishing them, holding inventory, and reselling them with warranties. It offers customers a more controlled experience, and many well-funded companies in India have pursued this approach. But it also ties up significant capital, exposes businesses to inventory depreciation, and becomes increasingly difficult to scale across fragmented markets.
The alternative is an asset-light marketplace. Instead of owning inventory, the platform connects buyers and sellers, and builds trust around the transaction. Margins may be thinner, but the model avoids inventory risk, requires far less capital, and can expand into new markets much more quickly.
OneClickDrive chose the second path, and that decision shapes much of its business.
Building trust instead of inventory
A marketplace succeeds only if it solves the problems that prevent transactions from happening. For used cars, those problems are finding the right vehicle and trusting the person selling it.
OneClickDrive used cars operates as a listings-only marketplace. It brings together thousands of vehicles from dealers and private sellers, displays prices upfront, and allows buyers to contact sellers directly by phone or message.
The platform does not set prices, own inventory, or process payments. Instead, it focuses on the trust layer: transparent listings, clear seller information, and a browsing experience built around comparison rather than lock-in.
That offers an important lesson for fragmented, low-trust markets. Competitive advantage doesn't necessarily come from owning inventory; it comes from creating enough trust and liquidity. OneClickDrive has done that without carrying a warehouse of depreciating assets.
Why supply matters more than demand
One of the less obvious lessons from marketplace businesses is that they are often won on the supply side. Buyers tend to arrive once there is enough quality inventory. Sellers are harder to attract because they are sensitive to listing fees, commissions and unnecessary friction.
OneClickDrive has focused on making selling as simple as possible. Listing is free, there are no commissions, and automation allows sellers to move from deciding to sell to publishing a live listing in minutes. Its proposition behind sell any car in Dubai reflects that approach: sellers pay nothing to list their vehicles while gaining immediate visibility among active buyers.
That steady flow of inventory keeps buyers returning to the platform, creating the marketplace flywheel every platform hopes to achieve.
For Indian founders, the takeaway is straightforward. The biggest growth challenge may not be customer acquisition, ad spend, or SEO. It may be making the supply side simple enough that sellers choose the platform in the first place.
Looking beyond domestic demand
The model also demonstrates how marketplace businesses can expand beyond their original purpose
Dubai’s position as a regional trade hub means a domestic vehicle marketplace can also serve buyers sourcing inventory for export access across the Middle East, Africa and parts of Asia. The same listings infrastructure that supports both local consumers and international trade buyers.
For Indian mobility startups, this highlights another advantage of building a marketplace first. Once trust, liquidity, and listings are established, adjacent services such as export, financing, and insurance can be added without rebuilding the business from scratch.
The marketplace becomes the foundation on which additional services can be built.
Lessons for Indian founders
The OneClickDrive model offers several takeaways for India's used car ecosystem.
First, founders should question whether owning inventory is essential. Managed inventory can improve the customer experience, but it also ties up capital and increases operational complexity. In fragmented markets, capital efficiency can become a stronger competitive advantage over time.
Second, trust should be treated as the core product rather than an additional feature. Transparent pricing, detailed listings, and direct buyer-seller communication are essential in markets where confidence remains a barrier to transactions.
Third, winning the seller matters as much as winning the buyer. Free, fast, and frictionless listing helps build the supply that attracts demand.
Finally, marketplaces should be designed with future expansion in mind. Once the listings and user base are established, services such as financing, insurance, and can be added as natural extensions of the platform.
OneClickDrive did not invent the online used car marketplace. What it demonstrated is how an asset-light model can scale in a market with strong supply, high transaction volumes, and clear incentives for buyers and sellers.
India’s used car market is still evolving. The two markets differ in important ways, but the UAE experience offers practical lessons for founders thinking about trust, liquidity, and sustainable growth.

articles.title: À seulement 75 €, ce clavier gaming MSI propose ce que la concurrence facture le double
articles.text:
| Type de clavier | Gaming | 
| Sans fil | Oui | 
| Format | TKL | 
| Pavé numérique | Non | 
| Type d'interrupteurs | Mécanique | 
| Rétroéclairage | Oui | 
Le MSI Forge GK600 TKL est un clavier gaming doté de switches linéaires. Il a la particularité de proposer des fonctionnalités habituellement réservées aux modèles plus coûteux, comme des commutateurs remplaçables à chaud et des capuchons de touches en PBT, tout en conservant un ticket d'entrée abordable.
Dans une industrie où tout devient plus cher ou moins bien fini qu'avant, un secteur se démarque depuis une demi-décennie en proposant de meilleurs produits à moindre coût : celui des périphériques PC, qu'il s'agisse des souris ou des claviers.
Là où un board custom pouvait facilement coûter près de 200 €, la multiplication des offres venues d'Asie a forcé les fabricants mainstream à diversifier leur catalogue pour séduire un public toujours plus exigeant. Il n'a jamais été aussi simple de s'équiper d'un clavier de qualité sans pour autant hypothéquer son logement.
C'est dans ce contexte que MSI commercialise le Forge GK600 TKL, un clavier au nom barbare (à l'acronyme évoquant pourtant l'excellence), mais à la proposition simple : un modèle inspiré du custom, hotswap et taillé pour le jeu, sous la barre des 100 €. Comme son appellation l'indique, il fait l'impasse sur le pavé numérique, mais s'offre le petit luxe d'un mini-écran LCD dans son coin supérieur droit, dont l'utilité concrète sera détaillée au cours de notre test. Le MSI Forge GK600 TKL est commercialisé à un tarif oscillant autour des 75 €.
Le MSI Forge GK600 TKL testé ici s'affiche dans son coloris Sky avec une base blanche agrémentée de nuances de bleu sur les touches ZQSD, secondaires et de fonction. Le mélange a le mérite d'être original et relativement discret face à des concurrents aux looks bien plus ostentatoires, sans être toutefois des plus harmonieux.
Néanmoins, la sérigraphie propre aux produits de la marque MSI trahit d'emblée son utilité première. On regrette que certaines touches soient difficiles à distinguer du premier coup d'œil, comme sur l'îlot latéral gauche – un point sur lequel nous reviendrons plus tard.
La construction du châssis en plastique est somme toute classique et attendue pour un produit sur ce segment tarifaire. Deux pieds latéraux offrant deux niveaux d'inclinaison permettent d'ajuster l'angle d’utilisation, le clavier disposant d'un profil haut qui s'avère fatigant pour les poignets au bout d'une demi-heure d'utilisation… L'inclusion d'un repose-poignets aurait été préférable, mais cela reste cohérent au vu du ticket d'entrée. Du reste, ses dimensions sont classiques pour un clavier TKL (34,8 x 14 x 4,5 cm), mais son poids est particulièrement notable puisqu'il frôle le kilogramme (943 g). Un modèle destiné avant tout à la sédentarité, donc.
Les regards les plus aiguisés parmi nos lecteurs auront remarqué la présence d'un mini-écran LCD de 1,06 pouce dans la partie supérieure droite du clavier, niché dans une alcôve. Une fois le Forge GK600 TKL allumé, il affiche une illustration statique tout à fait mignonne du petit dragon mascotte de la marque taïwanaise — de son nom de baptême Lucky, si vous insistez —, ainsi qu'une rangée d'icônes d'information sur les fonctionnalités du clavier, comme la connectivité sollicitée ou l'état de la batterie.
C'est via plusieurs combinaisons avec la touche Fn (arborant le logo dragon sur le Forge GK600, pour information) que l'on parcourt les différents menus de personnalisation intégrés, comme les motifs de rétroéclairage, son intensité ou le contrôle du volume sonore.
Il sert ainsi d'unique interface visuelle entre le clavier et l'utilisateur, puisque le MSI Forge GK600 TKL est l'un de ces rares modèles modernes à ne disposer d'aucun logiciel dédié fourni par le fabricant, ni même d'une compatibilité avec les gestionnaires de firmware open source comme QMK. Une approche qui limite considérablement la polyvalence de l'appareil, là où certains constructeurs, même les plus modestes, s'appuient sur des solutions open source pour la réassignation des touches. Ainsi, le clavier se dispense également de tout bouton dédié aux macros ou au multimédia.
Clavier gaming oblige, le Forge GK600 TKL profite d'un rétroéclairage RGB offrant un total de 20 motifs disponibles. Une proposition complète, mais limitée par une sérigraphie des touches totalement opaque qui ne laisse pas transparaître la lumière ; autant dire que dans le noir le plus total, mieux vaut être adepte du touch typing. On apprécie néanmoins l'utilisation de plastique PBT (polytéréphtalate de butylène) pour les capuchons de touches, ce qui préserve la sérigraphie bien plus longtemps que le plastique ABS. Notons que l'utilisation du rétroéclairage aura un impact substantiel sur la batterie : moins d'une semaine en utilisation "classique" lorsqu'il est activé. C'est assurément un board sédentaire...
Autre luxe surprenant, le Forge GK600 TKL propose trois modes de connectivité différents pour l'appairage : filaire via USB-C, Bluetooth et radio via le dongle 2,4 GHz. On note aussi une compatibilité macOS en plus de Windows. Pour basculer d'un mode à l'autre, la firme au dragon a placé différents interrupteurs sous le châssis, là où l'on a plutôt l'habitude de les trouver sur la tranche supérieure. En pratique, rares sont les moments où l'on a réellement besoin de changer de mode de connexion ou d'OS — l'emplacement est curieux, certes, mais acceptable. De plus, cette même face arrière intègre un logement de rangement pour le dongle USB-A, ce qui est toujours très appréciable.
MSI a fait le choix conservateur de ne proposer qu'une seule déclinaison pour ses commutateurs : des modèles linéaires. Plus précisément, il s'agit de KTT Purple Star, affichant une force d'activation de 43 g, une distance d'actionnement de 1,8 mm et une course totale de 4 mm, le tout sur une conception standard à cinq broches. Une caractéristique bienvenue, d'autant que le Forge GK600 TKL est hotswappable : le key puller (nos excuses pour tous ces anglicismes) fourni avec le board (encore désolé) permet de remplacer facilement les switches en cas de panne ou simplement pour personnaliser le clavier. Une fonctionnalité qui constitue un vrai plus, et a fortiori rare sur un produit de ce prix.
Non qu'il y ait à redire sur les switches fournis par défaut : la sensation de frappe est totalement linéaire, comme attendu, permettant d'enchaîner sans fatigue les parties de Counter-Strike, tandis que la frappe agréable confère au clavier une certaine polyvalence pour les tâches de bureautique grâce à une prélubrification efficace.
En bref, l'expérience de frappe réalise presque un sans-faute… Mais l'expérience utilisateur pâtit de l'absence du repose-poignets et du logiciel de personnalisation susmentionnés, ce qui explique la timide note de 3 étoiles accordée à cette sous-partie.
De plus, la disposition des touches sur l'îlot latéral gauche nous a laissé circonspect : là où les claviers TKL présentent (dans la grande majorité des cas) une disposition en deux rangées de trois colonnes, MSI se contente de deux colonnes et trois rangées tout en plaçant les touches PgUp et PgDn côte à côte, au lieu de les superposer comme le voudraient les usages habituels. À la place, on retrouve la touche Suppr au-dessus de la touche PgUp. Attention donc aux frappes accidentelles…
Attention à ne pas se fier aux apparences : derrière son ticket d'entrée abordable, le MSI FORGE GK600 TKL cache de sérieux atouts habituellement réservés aux claviers les plus chers. Avec sa compatibilité hot-swap, ses trois modes de connectivité, ses keycaps et ses switches de qualité, le clavier taïwanais se place en bonne porte d'entrée pour qui est intéressé par l'univers des boards custom. Avec toutefois quelques concessions attendues, notamment en termes de confort et de personnalisation.
Dans la catégorie des claviers gaming hotswap accessibles, on peut mentionner le Corsair K70 Pro Mini, qui commence à dater mais conserve un prix doux dans un format encore plus compact. Les boards Dark et Light Mount de Be Quiet! constituent aussi des options valables, bien que plus onéreuses.

articles.title: Este mapa te muestra todos los incendios activos de España en tiempo real, y puede avisarte si hay uno cerca de tu casa
articles.text:
Vamos a decirte qué es y cómo funciona incendiosespaña.es, una web con la que puedes ver todos los incendios activos en España. Así, ya estés planeando un viaje podrás saber si hay alguno en tu destino, y si lo tienes cerca de casa podrás recibir avisos si empieza a ser peligroso para ti.
Vamos a empezar explicándote qué es exactamente esta web, los datos que ofrece y de dónde obtiene su información. Después pasaremos a decirte cómo configurar un aviso para que te notifique cuando haya algún incendio que se acerque a tu casa.
Qué es IncendiosEspaña.es y de dónde saca los datos
Incendiosespaña.es es una página web que unifica y muestra en un mapa la información de todos los incendios que están teniendo lugar en España. Los muestra en un mapa donde puedes ver la cantidad de incendios, los focos activos, su ubicación e incluso su gravedad.
Los vas a tener todos en un mapa en el que vas a poder navegar a tu antojo, haciendo zoom en las zonas que te interesen y pulsando sobre los distintos iconos para ampliar la información. Hay iconos que te indican los incendios confirmados, y hay otros que te dicen los focos.
Cuando pulsas en uno de estos iconos vas a obtener datos como el tipo de incendios, el lugar donde están, los municipios afectados, e incluso la hora de inicio y los recursos asignados. También te va a dar otra información como su radio, la potencia radiativa (FRP), el nivel de confianza de la detección, carreteras cortadas, viento, y más.
Y en cuanto a las fuentes, la web obtiene los datos de los servicios de emergencias de varias comunidades autónomas, así como de los fotos de calor detectados por los satélites de NASA FIRMS, EUMETSAT y Copernicus/EFFIS. Esta información se actualiza casi en tiempo real, cada 5 minutos para los servicios públicos o 15 minutos para los satélites.
La web también tiene una columna izquierda donde puedes organizar los datos seleccionando el periodo de tiempo que quieres analizar o buscando poblaciones. También tienes una lista de focos por provincia con la que puedes navegar directamente hacia los que te interesan.
Cómo configurar las alertas
Si quieres configurar alertas para que se te avise si aparece un incendio cerca de tu casa, tienes que ir a la parte inferior de la pantalla. Cuando cierras el texto de cookies te aparecerá un mensaje donde se te invita a activar las alertas, y en él debes pulsar en el botón de Activar alertas.
Esto te va a llevar a una página web donde simplemente tienes que escribir tu correo electrónico, código postal y radio de aviso. Así, si aparece un incendio y la localidad perteneciente al código postal está dentro del radio de aviso que has configurado, se te enviará un mail con la alerta y diciéndote también tu nivel de riesgo.
